messages:
John C (acct-corp): Hey team — our customer integration started failing after we flipped on structured JSON (strict mode). API returns 400 "invalid response" and we can't parse the body. Example request:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-like-13b","structured_output": {"mode": "strict", "schema": "invoice"}, "prompt":"..."}'

We get 400 and the body looks valid JSON from the model but parsing fails in our client. Attaching two sample model outputs below.

John C (acct-corp): Sample A (fails parse):
{"id":"12345","total": 99.95,"active": null,"status":"Active"}

Sample B (works):
{"id": 12345,"total": 99.95,"active": true,"status":"ACTIVE"}

This looks like type/schema drift: id quoted vs numeric, active null vs boolean, and status casing. Can someone advise? Customer is blocked on billing import. :grimacing:

Marta S (support): Ack. Can you paste the exact API response body (raw) for one of the failures? Also which API client/sdk and version are you using? Any headers like X-Request-Id would help.

John C (acct-corp): Pasting raw response body (copied straight):
{"response":{"content":"{\"id\":\"12345\",\"total\":99.95,\"active\":null,\"status\":\"Active\"}"}}
Headers: X-Request-Id: rq_8z7a3
Client: our internal node wrapper v2.1.3

Marta S (support): Thanks. Tagging eng-ml to look — sounds like structured output strict parser is rejecting due to types. @Alex K @Ingrid L any ideas? :eyes:

Alex K (eng): Looking. Quick thought — strict mode expects exact types per schema. The model sometimes emits quoted numeric IDs when it samples. Also null vs omitted booleans cause issues. We can confirm by calling the same model with the same prompt.

Alex K (eng): Repro locally with the customer's prompt and strict schema; I hit same failure. The runtime returns content with id as string in some seeds. Example from our run:
{"id":"12345","total":99.95,"active":null,"status":"Active"}

Parser stacktrace (sanitized):
Error: StrictSchemaValidationError: field 'id' expected number but got string
  at StructuredParser.validate (/srv/runtime/parsers/strict.js:87)
  at /srv/runtime/request-handler.js:211

Ingrid L (eng-ml): Confirmed. This is a model sampling/decoding artifact: numeric-like tokens can be emitted with quotes depending on tokenization/context. For enums, casing differs because the model used natural capitalization. Two paths:
- Short term: support can transform model output before schema validation: coerce numeric strings to numbers, treat null/absent as false for boolean fields if schema allows, and normalize enum casing (uppercasing) — basically a tolerant pre-processor.
- Medium term: we can add a 'lenient_coercion' option on structured_output which will attempt coercions (quoted numbers, quoted booleans, enum case normalization) before strict validation.

Marta S (support): Customer needs a workaround now. John, would you be able to apply a preprocessing step on your side (coerce id to number if string, treat null active as false) as a short-term fix?

John C (acct-corp): We can add a quick post-parse shim in Node to coerce, but we'd prefer the platform to handle it since many customers hit this. Also worried about silently changing enums (could mask real issues).

Alex K (eng): Agreed about not hiding legit regressions. For now I recommend the shim + an SDK flag to enable coercion so it's opt-in. I'll open an internal ticket to add an explicit 'structured_output.lenient_coercion' boolean default false.

Support Bot: Ticket created: INF-8421 — "structured_output: lenient coercion option + better docs". Assigned to eng-ml. :spiral_note_pad:

Ingrid L (eng-ml): For immediate customer support I can add a temporary edge rule: if structured_output.mode == 'strict' and we detect numeric-in-strings we can attempt a single deterministic coercion and surface a warning in the response metadata (X-Structured-Coercion: id:string->number). That keeps strict validation but makes a safety net. Wanna try on John's request id rq_8z7a3?

John C (acct-corp): That would be ideal. Customer will accept a warning header. Thanks.

Marta S (support): @Alex can you schedule a small patch to enable that heuristic for rq_8z7a3? Then we can ask John to retry.

Alex K (eng): Pushed a hotfix to the request handler that applies deterministic coercion for numeric-looking strings, normalizes enum to upper-case for known enum fields, and treats null booleans as absent only for this request id. Deployed to prod cluster shard p-12.

Alex K (eng): Patch diff excerpt:
```
if (mode === 'strict') {
  if (typeof parsed.id === 'string' && /^\d+$/.test(parsed.id)) parsed.id = Number(parsed.id);
  if (parsed.status) parsed.status = parsed.status.toUpperCase();
  if (parsed.active === null) delete parsed.active; // prefer omission over null
}
```

John C (acct-corp): Retried — response now accepted by our parser. We see header X-Structured-Coercion: id:string->number,status:case-normalized,active:null->omitted. Customer is back online. :tada:

Marta S (support): Great. We'll leave INF-8421 open for the proper config/API flag and SDK support. Alex/Ingrid, please follow up with design doc and tests so we don't regress.

Ingrid L (eng-ml): Will do. I'll draft a short RFC: options (strict, lenient_coercion, permissive) + explicit warnings in response metadata and SDK opt-ins. ETA EOW.

John C (acct-corp): Thanks all for the quick turnaround!

Marta S (support): Closing interim loop — set me a PR link and we'll notify the customer once RFC is merged. :thumbsup:
